k.q: Apply AND logic to a simplified authentication and file-permission check.
k.code:
signedIn = true
allowedToRead = false
if signedIn AND allowedToRead then
    print("Access permitted")
else
    print("Access denied")
endif
p: Change allowedToRead to true and predict again.
Explain the difference between authentication and authorisation. Why does AND require both?
k.a: Initially Access denied. With both signedIn and allowedToRead true it prints Access permitted. Authentication establishes who a user is; authorisation checks what that user may access. AND requires both conditions. This is a simple access-rule model, not real authentication.

v: Output 1 only when both inputs are 1.
Output 1 when at least one input is 1.
Symbols and truth tables describe logic gate relationships independently of hardware.
x: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all its inputs are 1.
r: Explain why a bare 'faster' may fail to score an explanation mark.
It lacks the causal mechanism and scenario-specific improvement required by the question.
Explain why defragmentation can improve HDD access.
It places related fragments closer together, reducing mechanical seek time.
Explain one difference between LAN and WAN.
LAN covers smaller/local area; WAN connects over wide geographical areas.
Explain why MFA protects against a stolen password.
Even with a stolen password, the attacker lacks another required independent factor.
145.memoryCue: AND gate: Output 1 only when both inputs are 1.

challenge.coreHint: For AND, both conditions must be true. Being signed in is not the same as having permission.

stretch.task: Add an OR output to the same simplified access test and compare its result when signedIn=true but allowedToRead=false.
stretch.hint: Test signedIn AND allowedToRead, then signedIn OR allowedToRead. Discuss why the latter is unsafe for access control.
stretch.answer: AND is false and OR is true. Using OR for this rule could allow access when only one of the two required conditions holds.
